examples.question_text:
A cylindrical container has one open end, radius $3$ cm and height $7$ cm.
(a) Write an expression for its surface area using radius $r$ and height $h$.
(b) Calculate its surface area to $1$ decimal place.
examples.solution_text:
Count one circular base and the full curved surface.
(a) $A=\pi r^{2}+2\pi rh$.
(b) $\begin{align*} A&=\pi(3)^{2}+2\pi(3)(7)\\ &=9\pi+42\pi\\ &=51\pi\\ &\approx160.2\text{ cm}^{2}\end{align*}$

examples.question_text:
A thin cylindrical pipe is open at both ends. Its diameter is $12$ cm and its length is $24$ cm. Ignore the thickness of the material.
Find its surface area in exact form.
examples.solution_text:
$r=12\div2=6\text{ cm}$.
Both ends are open, so count only the curved surface.
$\begin{align*} A&=2\pi rh\\ &=2\pi(6)(24)\\ &=288\pi\text{ cm}^{2}\end{align*}$

The two semicircular ends together have area $\pi r^{2}$. The curved surface has area $\pi rh$.
The closed half-cylinder also has a flat top of area $2rh$.
$\begin{align*} A_{\text{closed}}&=\pi r^{2}+\pi rh+2rh\\ &=\pi(2)^{2}+\pi(2)(9)+2(2)(9)\\ &=22\pi+36\\ &\approx105.12\text{ cm}^{2}\end{align*}$
The open-top trough has no flat top.
$\begin{align*} A_{\text{trough}}&=\pi r^{2}+\pi rh\\ &=\pi(2)^{2}+\pi(2)(9)\\ &=22\pi\\ &\approx69.12\text{ cm}^{2}\end{align*}$
The difference is $2(2)(9)=36\text{ cm}^{2}$, the area of the flat rectangular top.

Count two quarter-circle ends, one quarter of the full curved surface and two rectangular cut faces.
$\begin{align*} A&=2\left(\frac14\pi r^{2}\right)+\frac14(2\pi rh)+2rh\\ &=\frac12\pi(4)^{2}+\frac12\pi(4)(11)+2(4)(11)\\ &=8\pi+22\pi+88\\ &=30\pi+88\\ &\approx182.25\text{ cm}^{2}\end{align*}$

Only half the full cylinder's curved surface remains.
$\begin{align*} A&=\frac12(2\pi rh)\\ &=\pi(6)(80)\\ &=480\pi\\ &\approx1508.0\text{ cm}^{2}\end{align*}$

examples.question_text:
A cylindrical swimming pool has diameter $4$ m and depth $1.2$ m. Its inside walls and floor need coating. One tin covers $6\text{ m}^{2}$.
How many whole tins are needed?
examples.solution_text:
$r=4\div2=2\text{ m}$.
Count the circular floor and curved walls.
$\begin{align*} A&=\pi r^{2}+2\pi rh\\ &=\pi(2)^{2}+2\pi(2)(1.2)\\ &=8.8\pi\text{ m}^{2}\end{align*}$
$\text{Number of tins}=8.8\pi\div6=4.607\ldots$.
Round up to cover the whole surface: $5$ tins.

coverage.summary: Authored six examples covering every distinct assessed method with changed values and the supplied face-by-face approach. Included editable cross-section diagrams where they clarify cuts and openings. Solutions use separate fields, aligned equations and renderer-inherited blue prose/math. Independent equations need no phantom equals. Assessments were classified only and remain unchanged. Final-size rendering verification remains for the capture stage.

examples.derivation: One circular base plus the full curved surface gives A = πr² + 2πrh. With r = 3 and h = 7, A = 9π + 42π = 51π = 160.2212… cm², hence 160.2 cm².
The radius is 12 ÷ 2 = 6 cm. Both ends are open, so A = 2πrh = 2π(6)(24) = 288π cm² exactly.

The semicircular ends total 4π cm² and the curved surface is 18π cm². The closed solid also has a 4 × 9 = 36 cm² rectangular top. Its area is 22π + 36 = 105.1150… cm², hence 105.12 cm². The trough area is 22π = 69.1150… cm², hence 69.12 cm². Their exact difference is the 36 cm² top.
Two quarter-circle ends total 8π cm². The quarter curved surface is 22π cm², and the two rectangular cut faces total 88 cm². A = 30π + 88 = 182.2477… cm², hence 182.25 cm².
With no top or end plates, only half the full curved surface remains. A = ½(2πrh) = π(6)(80) = 480π = 1507.9644… cm², hence 1508.0 cm².
The radius is 2 m. Floor and walls total π(2)² + 2π(2)(1.2) = 8.8π m². Required tins = 8.8π ÷ 6 = 4.6076…, so 5 whole tins are needed.

review.summary: All eight mapped methods and all 26 exact assessment locators are covered by the six examples. Diameter conversion is demonstrated in examples 1 and 5. No existing examples require dispositions. The examples follow the supplied face-counting method, use changed values and remain within scope. Prose stays editable outside mathematics and inherits solution blue. Aligned working has full opening equations, so no phantom equals gutter is needed. Cross-section diagrams contain givens only and use black ink with authored 10 pt labels. No syllabus exception is needed. Accepted assessment mathematics was not re-audited. Final-size rendering and label verification remain for the capture stage.
